title: Necessary to faith: each person’s explicit faith — or the Church’s public faith
source_text: IV. Et similiter aliquid ad fidem necessarium dicitur, vel quia necessarium est ad singulorum fidem, nec quisquam sine fide illius explicita fidelis censeri debet: vel in genere ad objectum fidei pertinet, & publicam fidem Ecclesiae obligat.
pass_a_gloss: And likewise something is said to be necessary to faith, either because it is necessary to the faith of individuals, and no one without explicit faith of that thing ought to be counted a believer: or because in general it pertains to the object of faith, and binds the public faith of the Church.
pass_b_english: So also ‘necessary to faith’ has two senses.
Either it is required for each person’s faith — no one without explicit faith in it should be counted a believer — or it belongs in general to faith’s object and binds the Church’s public faith.

choices.why: Opposed to implicit faith later in the tract.
